settings.name_in_paper: Finite-alpha alpha-Rank estimation from i.i.d. samples of each strategy profile
unmapped: Arms are strategy profiles of a K-player general-sum game; each query returns a vector of noisy payoffs (one per player)
Goal is to estimate the alpha-Rank invariant distribution within epsilon in sup norm
Non-adaptive: each profile sampled a fixed number N_s of times
settings.definition_quote: Let $\hat{\mathbf{M}}$ be an empirical payoff table constructed by taking $N_s$ i.i.d. interactions of each strategy profile $s \in S$. Then the invariant distribution $\hat{\boldsymbol{\pi}}$ derived from the empirical payoff matrix $\hat{\mathbf{M}}$ satisfies $\max_{s} |\pi(s) - \hat{\pi}(s) | \leq \varepsilon$

settings.name_in_paper: Infinite-alpha response-graph recovery with static sampling (known gap)
unmapped: Arms are strategy profiles of a K-player game; each query returns noisy payoffs for all players
Goal: exactly recover the infinite-alpha alpha-Rank transition matrix (response graph), i.e. signs of all single-player-deviation payoff differences
Non-adaptive sampling with N_s per profile chosen using the gap lower bound
settings.definition_quote: Suppose all payoffs are bounded in $[-M_\mathrm{max}, M_\mathrm{max}]$, and that ... $|\mathbf{M}^k(\sigma, s^{-k}) - \mathbf{M}^k(\tau, s^{-k})| \geq \Delta$ for all distinct $\sigma, \tau \in S^k$, for some $\Delta > 0$. ... the transition matrix $\hat{\mathbf{C}}$ computed from payoff table $\hat{\mathbf{M}}$ is exact

settings.name_in_paper: Adaptive response-graph identification (collection of pure-exploration bandit problems)
unmapped: Arms are strategy profiles of a K-player general-sum game; each query returns noisy payoffs for all players
Goal: determine, with confidence 1-delta, the sign of every payoff difference between profiles differing in one player's strategy (the response graph)
Instances with ties between compared payoffs are excluded
settings.definition_quote: We seek an algorithm which specifies (i) a sampling scheme $\mathcal{S}$ that selects the next strategy profile $s \in S$ for which a noisy game outcome is observed, and (ii) a criterion $\mathcal{C}(\delta)$ that stops the procedure and outputs the estimated payoff table used for the infinite-$\alpha$ \alpharank rankings, which is exactly correct with probability at least $1-\delta$.

settings.name_in_paper: Elo (BatchElo) estimation in symmetric two-player win-loss games with static sampling
unmapped: Arms are pairs of strategies in a symmetric two-player win-loss game
Goal: row sums of BatchElo fitted win probabilities within epsilon of those from the true payoff matrix
Non-adaptive: each pair sampled N_{s,s'} times
settings.definition_quote: Consider a symmetric, two-player win-loss game with finite strategy set $S^1$ and payoff matrix $\mathbf{M}$. Let $\mathbf{q}$ be the fitted payoffs obtained from the BatchElo model on the payoff matrix $\mathbf{M}$, and let $\hat{\mathbf{q}}$ be the fitted payoffs obtained from the BatchElo model on an empirical payoff table $\hat{\mathbf{M}}$

algorithms.name: Static uniform sampling (N_s i.i.d. interactions per profile) + alpha-Rank on empirical payoffs

bound.expression_latex: N_s > \frac{648 M_{\mathrm{max}}^2 \log(2|S|K/\delta) L(\alpha, M_\mathrm{max})^2 \left( \sum_{n=1}^{|S|-1} \binom{|S|}{n} n^{|S|} \right)^2 }{\varepsilon^2 g(\alpha, \eta, m, M_\mathrm{max})^2}

symbols.g_a: g(alpha, eta, m, M_max) = eta*(exp(2*alpha_r*M_max)-1)/(exp(2*alpha_r*m*M_max)-1), eta, m alpha-Rank parameters

tuning: alpha-Rank parameters alpha, m fixed (finite alpha)

Let $\hat{\mathbf{M}}$ be an empirical payoff table constructed by taking $N_s$ i.i.d. interactions of each strategy profile $s \in S$. Then the invariant distribution $\hat{\boldsymbol{\pi}}$ ... satisfies $\max_{s} |\pi(s) - \hat{\pi}(s) | \leq \varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, if N_s > ...

results.notes: Bound is a sufficient per-profile sample count N_s (total samples = |S| times this). Guarantee is sup-norm error epsilon on the alpha-Rank stationary distribution.

conditions: all single-player deviation payoff differences have magnitude at least Delta > 0

source.label: thm:sample_complexityinfinite
source.quote: Suppose all payoffs are bounded in $[-M_\mathrm{max}, M_\mathrm{max}]$, and that $\forall k \in [K]$ and $\forall s^{-k} \in S^{-k}$, we have $|\mathbf{M}^k(\sigma, s^{-k}) - \mathbf{M}^k(\tau, s^{-k})| \geq \Delta$ ... Then the transition matrix $\hat{\mathbf{C}}$ computed from payoff table $\hat{\mathbf{M}}$ is exact ... with probability at least $1-\delta$, if $N_s > 8\Delta^{-2}M_\mathrm{max}^2 \log(2|S|K/\delta)$

results.notes: Paper's Delta is a lower bound on all relevant payoff gaps (mapped to Delta_min). Per-profile sample count; total is |S| times.

tuning: confidence levels chosen so that per-interval failure f(u,delta,t) = 6 delta / (pi^2 |S| sum_k(|S^k|-1) t^3)

source.label: thm:adaptivecorrectness
source.quote: The {\responsegraphucb} algorithm is correct with high probability: Given $\delta \in (0,1)$, for any particular sampling scheme there is a choice of confidence levels such that ResponseGraphUCB outputs the correct response graph with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: delta-correctness statement: probability of outputting an incorrect response graph is at most delta.

conditions: Delta = minimum over single-player deviation pairs of the payoff difference, Delta > 0
tuning: Hoeffding confidence bounds with confidence parameter delta

source.quote: The {\responsegraphucb} algorithm, using confidence parameter $\delta$ and Hoeffding confidence bounds, run on an evaluation instance with $\Delta = \min_{(s^k, s^{-k}), (\sigma^k, s^{-k})} |\mathbf{M}^k(s^k, s^{-k}) - \mathbf{M}^k(\sigma^k, s^{-k})|$ requires at most $\mathcal{O}(\Delta^{-2} \log(1/(\delta\Delta)))$ samples with probability at least $1-2\delta$.

results.notes: Holds with probability at least 1-2delta. Proof shows this is the per-profile sample count; dependence on M_max, |S| and number of players hidden in O. No LaTeX label on this theorem.

symbols.n_strat: number of strategies |S^1| of the symmetric two-player game

source.label: thm:elo_complexity
source.quote: If we take, for each pair of strategy profiles $s, s^\prime \in S^1$, a number of interactions $N_{s, s^\prime}$ satisfying $N_{s, s^\prime} > 0.5|S^1|^2 \varepsilon^{-2} \log(|S^1|^2/\delta )$. Then it follows that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\left|\sum_{s^\prime} ( \mathbf{q}_{s, s^\prime} - \hat{\mathbf{q}}_{s, s^\prime} ) \right| < \varepsilon$ for all s.

results.notes: Per-pair sample count; guarantee on row sums of Elo-fitted win probabilities.
